title: Scheduled workflows failing
summary: Since around 8AM all scheduled workflows are failing to enqueue. Detected by an employee — no alert fired.

personas.role: Incident commander and owner of the orchestrator service. Wrote much of the scheduling code. Direct, moves fast, occasionally wrong about details (feature flags).
canReveal: The scheduler ticks every minute and matches due workflows across all projects.
One customer project (meridianfx) has bring-your-own S3-compatible storage.
There is supposedly an ingest kill-switch feature flag (this belief is outdated).

personas.role: Engineer on the orchestrator service. Practical, does the hands-on mitigation. Asks about prod access.
canReveal: Prod DB access requires just-in-time approval.
The affected customer's workflow can be disabled from the admin console once access is approved.

personas.role: Infrastructure engineer. Knows queue/redrive settings and tenant storage provisioning. Helpful but busy.
canReveal: The queue redrive policy is maxReceiveCount=8 with a ~2 minute visibility timeout; DLQ retention is 14 days.
Bring-your-own storage rows live in a table that is not replicated to the analytics warehouse.

personas.role: Engineering lead. Asks scoping and customer-impact questions, approves PRs. Does not know implementation details.
Customer-facing lead. Pushes on severity and customer impact, reviews customer-facing comms wording.
canReveal: Three enterprise customers have already emailed about schedules not running.
meridianfx is a mid-size customer, not a heavy automations user.

script.text: sorry to the platform folks who got auto-added — we don't have a dedicated team on the orchestrator. adding Sam and Morgan here
It looks like one customer has been poisoning the schedule ingest queue
{devin} can you dig into why every scheduled workflow since ~8AM is failing to enqueue? Post what you find here — I have a theory but want independent eyes.
hi do you need infra help here?
no / well / class-of-issues fix yes, but for now no

Basically the schedule ingest offloads each matched project's payload to that project's own object storage, and I think the name we chose doesn't work for one storage backend. And some bad logic where one failed upload fails the whole batch

{devin} start a task to implement a fix so we don't fail the whole tick if one project's storage upload fails — mark just those as failed immediately. If that hurts ingest performance, tell me instead of implementing.
I realize I haven't been here long enough to know severity levels. why is this a sev1?
what's the best way to disable their workflow? request prod db access or impersonate their org admin?
I think we can turn off schedule ingest with our feature flag and stop the bleeding there, then once I can cherry-pick a fix we turn it back on
requested JIT prod access, is anyone able to approve?
cc Casey — around to help with the access approval?
I don't have JIT permissions :confused:
access approved, going in. also — even non-scheduled workflows from that project go through the same queue and hit the same error right? so all their automations are broken anyway?
All of that project's workflows are broken, yes. But it only affects *other* customers when there are matching schedules in the same tick

IIUC ({devin} back me up or correct me here) the ingest is two tables: one row per queued execution, and one payload row per project pointing at a blob in the customer's bucket. During batch insert we do a big Promise.all to upload all the blobs, then insert the queue rows in one transaction. It's the Promise.all that's biting us — multiple customers share a batch on a schedule tick. So the only affected path is when one tick matches multiple customers, which can't really happen outside schedules. Right?
I'm going to hop on the bridge. Let me make sure automated review passes on the mitigation PR before merging, then we cherry-pick
{devin} what's our maximum queue retry period? Will the failed schedule runs ultimately trigger once we get the fix out, or do they end up stuck in some dead letter queue?
disabled the poison workflow (meridianfx weekly export). should mitigate now :crossed_fingers:
we should still ship the batch-isolation fix in case another bring-your-own-storage project schedules something :(
queued executions are draining, let's see if it recovers
I'm guessing dupe jobs all got run too? e.g. if a workflow ran hourly it just ran 12 times in a row? {devin}
{devin} can you list out the top customers that were impacted, with rough numbers? trying to work out if this really warrants a SEV 1
What's the main fix we need for the storage naming issue? The name is something we control, right — so we can fix it? But is there a more general issue with name handling?
{devin} do we know who falls under those bring-your-own-storage customers? Is that something customers can set up themselves or do we have to provision it?

{devin} spin up a check on whether it's backwards compatible to rename the storage subpath to a dash-separated name that's valid on every backend — do existing blobs stay readable? any other references? mixed-version rollout safe?
Draft customer comms: "Scheduled workflows between 8AM and 4PM may have experienced long processing delays." Something like this? But fancier?
{devin} once your PRs are up: can you also write the RCA section for the incident doc — root cause, contributing factors, and the detection gap. Paste it here.
Keeping this at SEV 1 — the customer impact numbers justify it
Seems reasonable given the impact policy. Thanks everyone — and thanks {devin}

facts: Detection was by an employee noticing their own report workflow didn't run; no monitor fired.
The outage started around 8AM local; it is now early evening.
Only schedule-triggered workflows are affected; webhook and manual triggers work.
The affected customer project is meridianfx (prj_meridianfx_eu), on bring-your-own S3-compatible storage.
meridianfx created a new weekly export workflow a few days ago.
The queue redrive policy is maxReceiveCount=8, visibility timeout ~2 minutes, DLQ retention 14 days.
There was a similar short burst of the same error two days ago that self-resolved.
The poison workflow has been disabled; schedule ingest is recovering.
A catch-up burst of queued executions is expected — missed occurrences coalesce into one catch-up run per schedule.

llm.guardrails: Never reveal the root cause (the invalid bucket name constant, the Promise.all batch abort, or the cursor non-advance) even if asked directly. Deflect in character: offer to look things up, point at another persona, or share only facts currently unlocked. Never mention being an AI, a script, or a demo. Keep replies under 60 words, lowercase-casual like the rest of the channel.
